title: Nelson Mandela
examples: What was the main cause of the conflict in South Africa?
What does 'reconciliation' mean in the context of his life?
Can you tell me more about the struggle against Apartheid?

explain.say: Nelson Mandela fought against a system called Apartheid.
This system kept people apart based on their skin colour.
He spent twenty-seven long years in prison for his activism.
After his release, he became the first Black president of South Africa.
His goal was to bring peace through reconciliation, not revenge.
In everyday life, we see this when communities work together after a disagreement.

faq.q: How long was Nelson Mandela in prison?
faq.a: He spent twenty-seven years in prison for his fight for freedom.
asks: How many years did he serve?
What was the length of his imprisonment?

faq.a: Apartheid was a harsh system of racial segregation in South Africa.
asks: Can you explain the system of Apartheid?

faq.a: It means making peace and rebuilding trust between groups that were fighting.
asks: Is reconciliation just forgetting the past?
What is the goal of reconciliation?

faq.q: Who was the first Black president of South Africa?
faq.a: Nelson Mandela achieved this important role after the end of Apartheid.
asks: What was his first presidential title?

faq.q: Did he want revenge after being released?
faq.a: No, he strongly believed in reconciliation and working toward peace.
asks: Was he interested in fighting again?
What was his approach after prison?

facts: Apartheid was a system of institutionalised racial segregation.
Nelson Mandela spent twenty-seven years in prison.
He became the first Black president of South Africa.
His leadership focused on reconciliation and peace.

quiz.say: The system that enforced racial separation in South Africa was called:
quiz.why: Apartheid was the specific name for the laws enforcing racial separation.

wrong.1: Segregation is the general act of keeping groups apart, but Apartheid was the specific law.
wrong.2: Racism is prejudice, but Apartheid was the government system that enforced it.
wrong.3: Oppression is the act of keeping someone down, but Apartheid was the name of the system.

quiz.say: Mandela's focus after his release was on:
quiz.why: Reconciliation means trying to heal divisions and build peace between groups.

wrong.0: Isolation would keep people apart, which is the opposite of his goal.
wrong.1: While resistance was necessary, reconciliation was his goal for the future.
wrong.3: Seeking revenge would restart conflict instead of ending it.

quiz.say: The period of racial laws and separation in South Africa is known as:
quiz.why: Apartheid is the precise historical term for the laws governing racial separation.

wrong.0: While true, Apartheid is the recognized name for the entire system.
wrong.2: Colonialism is a broader term for one country ruling another.
wrong.3: Jim Crow laws were a similar system, but they were specific to the United States.
